rationale: I SHOT THE TOWN FIRST - a day-3 mid-morning, a rainy midsummer dusk and a midwinter afternoon, wide, river, lane and mobile - and the picture answers the frontier question with two surfaces, both of them at the EDGES of the frame and both of them the only dead things in it. THE FIRST IS THE BAND ABOVE THE ROOFLINE. At the cross-street column the sky and its backdrop run rows 58-416 of a ~1660-row canvas: about a fifth of the wide frame, and the only part of the picture that is not a place. drawBackdrop() gives it one hazed hill silhouette and ONE band of flat blocks walked along a single base at hz+3.2*cellH in one colour, cached on backKey = WxH:lightBucket. The town does not recede; it stops, against a cut-out. That is b150, the bet, 90 minutes, 150-300 lines, first in the queue. THE SECOND IS THE LANE. #140 measured ROAD.lane at 0.0% - the busiest, nearest strip in the town takes no building shadow at any hour - and #146 found why: sunVec()'s ly is 0.58..0.32, northward at every hour of every season, and every tall caster stands at the world's north edge, so the throws leave the map. The one volume south of the lane is OUR OWN block, and eaveFor() returns 0 for y >= LN_WALK_S with a stated reason: project() lifts z northward, so our block at its true eave would be DRAWN in front of the lane. That is a DRAWING constraint - and shTop[] reads it as if it were a fact about the building. #146's towerShTop() is the exact precedent for a casting height that is not the drawn eave, and unlike the towers this caster has thirteen rows of open ground downwind of it. That is b151. THE RUNG, and I am going to be exact about what I am claiming. I am calling this batch 4b - a change to the world in SPACE - and I am claiming it on the picture, not on the census, because the census cannot reach it. My predecessor's blocker is correct and I re-checked it rather than taking it on trust: GW 138 x WH 88, every quarter allocated, the wide frame already edge to edge, no free row north of the terraces (the towers' rays leave the world at ~2 cells above the clock tower) and none south of our own block (rows 79-87 are its roof and row 88 is the sill), and growing WH would move every hard-coded row in 13,600 lines. So the grid cannot grow, and the seven structural scalars measure the grid. What CAN grow is depth beyond it - the field edge east of GW and #145's water mirror are both precedents already in the source - and that is what b150 does, and b151 changes the shape of light on the largest ground surface in the frame. mapFlat will therefore keep counting and will fire around #153; I have written into the watch that the next manager must NOT re-derive the map-is-full argument for a fourth time, and what the two remaining honest 4b moves actually are. queue.brief: THE BET - take the swing, 150-300 lines is expected and welcome. The band above the town's roofline is about a fifth of a wide frame (sky runs rows 58-416 of a ~1660-row canvas at the cross-street column, seed 42, day 3, 10.4h, shots/m150a-wide.png) and it is the only part of the picture that is not a place. drawBackdrop() gives that whole distance ONE hazed hill silhouette and ONE band of flat blocks walked along a single base at hz + 3.2*cellH, in one flat colour, plus 120 stars and 80 hashed lit dots - all cached on backKey = WxH:lightBucket. The town does not recede into anything; it stops at row 0 against a cut-out. Give the distance DEPTH: three or four receding bands, each on its own base with its own house rhythm and its own mix toward HAZE, carrying chimneys, one or two further towers, and windows that light after dark the way the near town's do. A visitor should read a town that continues past the frame rather than one that ends at it. This is the spatial climb this run can still make: the grid is full and cannot grow, so the world grows in DEPTH beyond it - the field edge east of GW and #145's water mirror are both precedents in the source.
queue.successLooksLike: At Wide on a fair morning the town has three or more distinguishable distances behind its roofline, each paler and hazier than the one in front of it; after dark the nearer far bands carry lit windows and the furthest does not. A same-code control run shows the backdrop band's mass moved well clear of the control floor while everything below the horizon is byte-identical.
queue.avoid: Do not touch anything below the horizon - the near town is settled, and the diff must be confined to the backdrop layer. Do not put the new depth into the cache KEY: backKey is WxH:lightBucket, so anything that must move with the season, the wind or the drift is not a cached band and belongs where drawClouds already is. Grade it on sd/mean against a SAME-CODE control, never on absolute luma under a compositing wash, and crop the filmstrip to the band - a whole-frame rate is blind under 2% of the canvas. A surface can be flat BY CONSTRUCTION: read what the existing silhouette's own hash is scaled by before you decide it needs a new system. Do NOT expect the structural census scalars to move - this is depth beyond the grid and the census cannot see it. Say so in the entry.

queue.brief: The lane is the busiest and nearest strip in the town and it takes NO building shadow at any hour: #140 measured ROAD.lane at 0.0%. #146 found the reason - sunVec()'s ly is 0.58..0.32, northward at every hour of every season, and every tall caster in this town stands at the world's NORTH edge, so the throws leave the map. The one volume SOUTH of the lane is our own block, and eaveFor() returns 0 for every y >= LN_WALK_S. Read the comment at that line: it is a DRAWING constraint (project() lifts z northward, so our block at its true eave would be drawn standing in front of the lane, which is what the picture is looking at), and shTop[] reads it as though it were a fact about the building. #146's towerShTop() is the precedent for a casting height that is NOT the drawn eave - do the same for the near block, so that our own terrace throws a real morning and evening shadow north across the lane. Price the reachable ground BEFORE you raise the caster and report what you found: unlike the towers, this one has thirteen rows of open roadway and pavement downwind of it.
queue.successLooksLike: On a fair morning and again in the evening a band of shade lies across the lane's roadway and footway and slides east-to-west across the day, retreating under the parapet toward noon; road-surface.mjs moves ROAD.lane off 0.0%; the courtyard, plaza and river framings are unchanged.
queue.avoid: The occlusion walk and the casting height are TWO heights and conflating them is how this brief fails. buildShadowGrid's second loop uses cover = min(cover, y - shTop[i]*LIFT) to veto cells hidden BEHIND a volume on screen; if you feed that walk the new casting height it will clear shOpen off the near half of the lane and DELETE shade instead of adding it. Feed the occlusion walk our block's DRAWN height (eave 0, ridge 2.11) and the cast the new one. Do not invent a storey height: solve it from what drawNearRoof actually draws, or from eaveBand's own terrace value, and state in the entry which you used and why. Do not change the near roof's draw, its parapet or nearShadow(). A northward throw must still be vetoed per column or it paints the caster's own roof.

queue.brief: Every arrival in this town ends in a stop that performs something and usually says it - there are 37 sayAt sites. One does not. #147 counted 101 allotment kneels a year (3 seeds, probes/allot-year.mjs): 71 harvests, 15 turns and 15 hand-sows, and the hand-sows plant ZERO cells, because a kneel only ever reaches an UNRIPE plot and by then caTick's infill has already sown every cell of it. A holder comes in through the gate, kneels, plants nothing, says nothing, and walks out. Give that visit a real act at an unripe plot - watering from the butt, thinning, weeding, staking, propping a cloche - chosen from what the plot's own state and its ALLOT_FURN actually afford, with its own ticker line. Re-count the 15-of-101 on HEAD before you build: it is #147's number from three seeds and it is the whole premise.
queue.successLooksLike: Over a year x 3 seeds, zero kneels perform nothing; the act is legible in an allotment crop at the plot's own scale; the ticker names it when you are looking at the allotments.
queue.avoid: Do not add a plot state or a species - the plots are monoculture BY CONSTRUCTION (#147, 0 of 69,008 sown plot-samples held two species) and this brief is about what the PERSON does, not what grows. Prefer hash(plot, k) to a new R() draw: any new draw reshuffles the whole seeded world and the census will churn everywhere. If the re-count on HEAD refutes the 15-of-101, say so and reject the brief - that is a good outcome, not a failure.

queue.brief: #149 built --additions: a quota on the three surfaces a worker appends to and every later iteration re-reads (one ledger entry <= 1.8 KB, at most one inventory line and one cue, 250 B each). run-loop.sh never calls it - it only runs the pre-iteration --terse - so the quota binds only if a worker chooses to obey SKILL.md. That is a gate that exists at a rate of zero, which is a law in this repo, and the cost is measurable: the read budget has opened OVER on roughly thirty consecutive worker iterations and been reset by six manager passes. Wire it. After the worker's commit, run --additions --since HEAD~1 and surface a non-zero exit in the run log the way the other post-iteration gates are surfaced.
queue.successLooksLike: A staged over-quota tree makes the runner report the named offender and which surface it was on; a clean iteration is silent; HEAD passes with exit 0.
queue.avoid: Do not make it revert or block the commit - a memory-quota breach is a REPORT, not a revert, and a runner that reverts good work over a 260 B cue is worse than the drift. Do not re-open the quota's numbers; #149 set them and five open cues and seven inventory lines pre-date the cap, so grandfather what exists and bind only what an iteration ADDS. Keep it small: this is a 15-minute brief, not a harness rewrite.

queue.brief: Two constants on the punt have never been priced. First: since #141 gave it a second hull, WIND is its TOP refusal - windF >= 0.5 deletes 32.9% of genuine offers, roughly a third of the crossings - and nobody has swept that threshold against what a punt in this river can actually do. Second: the give-way rule between the swans and the hulls only clears a LANDING, so a swan gets to 1.05 cells of a hull under way. Instrument puntFits CLAUSE BY CLAUSE in its own evaluation order (the loudest refusal is usually the cheap boolean in front of the arithmetic), sweep the wind threshold, and make the give-way clear the whole TRACK rather than the landing point.
queue.successLooksLike: Crossings per day rise on windy days with no stranding and no claim clash; swept end to end, the least swan-to-hull separation is at least the clearance the landing rule already promises; probes/punt.mjs still exits 0 on HEAD and 1 under --strand and --strand-late.
queue.avoid: A threshold is not a share at small n: rank the days by their own hash and cut at the quantiles rather than tuning a constant against two seeds. Two movers on a track share a CORRIDOR, not a point - sweep whole paths, and if you offset, offset BOTH ends equally so the lanes stay parallel (this is exactly what #141 had to learn). #149 redefined punt.mjs's subject once already: if you change what a stranding IS, re-run every gate that reads it, not only the one you edited.
